blob_select — BLOB select op

• Data kinds: labels2d → labels2d

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.blob_select(labels: 'Any', feature: 'str', vmin: 'Optional[float]' = None, vmax: 'Optional[float]' = None, spacing: 'float' = 1.0) -> 'np.ndarray' (to call the implementation directly, import blob2d; blob2d.blob_select(labels: 'Any', feature: 'str', vmin: 'Optional[float]' = None, vmax: 'Optional[float]' = None, spacing: 'float' = 1.0) -> 'np.ndarray'; from the registry, opsblob.get("blob_select"))

Usage

Keeps only the objects whose feature value lies in [vmin, vmax] (the numbers are reassigned starting from 1).

Parameters

labels : array_like

Output of blob_label.

feature : str

One of FEATURE_KEYS. An unknown key is rejected, with the candidates listed.

vmin, vmax : float or None

Both ends (inclusive). None leaves that side open. Both None means

"nothing selected" and is rejected -- if you intend to pass everything, just do not call it.

spacing : float

Same meaning as in blob_features. Needed when cutting area or perimeter

in physical units.

Returns

numpy.ndarray

int32 label image. The surviving objects are renumbered consecutively 1..k

(the original numbers are not kept). If you need the original numbers, take

blob_features(labels)["label"] beforehand.
